messages:
alex: FYI - new intel from vendor: OpenSSL and glibc fixes landed for ubuntu:22.04 and alpine:3.18. We need a remediation approach for our base images. Do we backport packages for existing images or trigger a full rebuild with updated upstream distros?

jamal: CVEs? can you drop IDs so we can triage severity?

sec-bot: CVE-2026-3456, CVE-2026-3457, link: https://security.example.com/advisories/2026-3456 (vendor advisory). Both rated HIGH; one has exploitability score >7.

maria: TL;DR: OpenSSL fix is source-level but packaged in libssl3/libcrypto packages. glibc fix touches NSS/crypt setups and could affect static-linked binaries. Prioritize images that run inference runtime and any customer-facing CLI.

alex: Agreed. Suggested prioritization: (1) runtime-prod images (GPU nodes), (2) API gateway containers, (3) build containers and dev images. Any objections?

devex: Please also consider developer workflow impact: some teams rely on distro versions for local dev. If we rebuild to latest 22.04 point release, there may be minor libc ABI deltas for C extensions. We should run integration tests for pip wheels that build native extensions.

jamal: For short-term patching we can do: apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade libssl3 libc6 on existing images and push a patch tag. For Alpine: apk add --upgrade libssl3 musl. But that won't change underlying rootfs snapshots; wonder about layering implications for our image signing pipeline.

sre-ops: Plan sketch for rollout: 
- Create patched image tags: rwd-runtime:2026.04-patch01 (apply only-upgrade)
- Run canary on 5% GPU pool 
- 24h perf+smoke checks (latency, memory, KV cache refill)
- If green, promote to 30% then full.
We need to run kernel compatibility tests too (glibc-lto edge cases).

claudia: We should sign patched images and update SBOMs. Also add an audit-log entry (RBAC scope: image-promotion role) before promoting. Who's owning the signing step? @devex?

devex: I can wire the CI job for signing but need an RBAC tweak: current CI service account can't call KMS/attestation for images in prod. @sec-bot can you confirm required permission list?

sec-bot: Required perms: kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign, containeranalysis.notes.attach, storage.objects.create (for signed layers), plus iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the CI account. I'll open a PR in infra-iam for a scoped role.

maria: Also add these checks before promotion: 
- Repro build test (from our build pipeline)
- Fuzz small native extension test matrix (numpy, tokenizers)
- Nightly eval-run for a sanity prompt set
- Compare tokenization outputs between old/new images (to catch subtle locale/glibc changes)

jamal: Quick snippet for the patch job (CI):
```bash
docker run --rm -v /var/lib/apt/lists:/tmp/apt-lists ubuntu:22.04 /bin/bash -lc '\n  apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade -y libssl3 libc6 && dpkg -l | grep -E "libssl|libc6"\n'
```
We will rebuild a minimal image if any package can't be upgraded in-place.

alex: Good. If we need full rebuilds, what cadence? I suggest fast track: runtime + gateway rebuilt within 48h; other images next 7 days.

sre-ops: We'll need canary capacity booked; SRE to reserve 2 GPU nodes for canary for the next 72h window. I'll file a ticket.

claudia: On auditing: add an immutable audit trail entry in ELA for the patch, include CVEs, package versions, image digest, signer, and KMS key. Also include a pointer to the rollback image digest. This should be in the release notes template.

devex: Anybody run into downstream breakage when glibc moved from 2.35->2.36 in past? We should watch for TLS handshake failures with certain crypto backends.

maria: Past incident: a linking mismatch caused tokio-rs native lib to fail in one service — manifested as intermittent TLS negotiation errors. Good to include a TLS smoke test hitting a known public endpoint that exercises SNI + client certs.

jamal: Can we add a canary fallback policy? If new image reports >0.5% 5xxs or p99 latency regression >10% for 15m, auto-roll back to previous digest. We have the rollout controller with that capability.

alex: Yes, add rollout policy to canary manifest. Also create an incident channel template so on rollback we notify customers and sales.

sre-ops: I'll author the canary manifest change and push to infra repo. Example config snippet: 
```yaml
canary:
  percent: 5
  checks:
    - type: smoke
      failure_threshold: 0.5
    - type: latency
      p99_threshold: 1.10
  rollback: true
```

devex: For CI gating, add: build -> unit tests -> native wheel smoke -> docker patch step -> signing -> integration smoke -> canary promote. Any approvals required for production? I propose security approves for runtime images.

claudia: Security approval via the "image-promotion" workflow group. We'll tag PRs with `sec-approve` and the infra-iam change will add the group.

maria: Last note: create a vulnerability dashboard card with affected images + CVE status + mitigation state (patched/backported/rebuilt) and link in the incident ticket.

alex: Ok, action items: 
- jamal: script & patch tags (ETA: 4h)
- devex: CI signing job + update service account perms (ETA: EOD)
- sre-ops: canary capacity + manifest (ETA: 6h)
- claudia: audit entry template + approval flow (ETA: EOD)
- maria: test matrix & TLS smoke tests (ETA: 12h)
I'll consolidate plan and open a tracking ticket. Thanks everyone :+1:

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-88: "OpenSSL/glibc patch sweep - ubuntu22.04/alpine3.18" and linked CVEs.
